species: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae (New England aster), straight species, no cultivar
note: Draft ground truth written 2026-11-27 by a research agent, blind to model code. Stats left for the orchestrator. peakAge 4 is a tolerance: no source gives a time to maturity for the straight species; sources say large clumps, and USDA advises dividing every 3 years to keep vigor. peakDay 266 is 23 Sep, the median-week (39) of iNaturalist annotated flowering in Ohio. Karen's chart row (3-6 ft, blooms Aug-Oct, medium to wet, sun to part shade) agrees with the sourced overlap on height and months; the Ohio photo record peaks later than August (weeks 36-41 hold 80 percent of annotated observations), so August is an early, thin shoulder. No source gives stems, heads or shoot counts per clump by age, and no mature-clump photograph could be counted, so there is NO stems or heads check; they are listed as needs-a-human in the report. Age 0 first-year flowering conflicts between sources (a volunteer botanical atlas, bplant.org: flowers, few blooms, usually one stem, a fraction of mature height; a nursery text: seed-grown blooms in year 2); no reputable source says, so no absent/flower check at age 0. Leaf litter speed is unknown (no source), treated as slow per the rules. The winterLeaves share is a tolerance set from one winter photograph (Delaware OH, 4 Feb 2026) in which dead brown leaves hang on the standing stems, so less than all leaf mass lies low. PROXY FOLLOW-UP 2026-11-27: no related aster was rated a close match (swamp aster, smooth blue aster and New York aster are partial; aromatic and calico aster are poor), so no check rests on a proxy alone; proxies are only named in proxySupport fields. Owner fact: her plant was set out in spring 2026 as a one-year-old, so it is age 1 in Nov 2026, did not bloom in 2026, and was browsed.

Quantiles of observation counts, week 10/25/50/75/90 percent: all years 36/37/39/40/41; 2021-2025 36/37/38/40/41, so no clear shift. iNaturalist week numbers may be off by one against floor((day-1)/7)+1. visual: Judged by eye, no number: leaves clasp the stem with ear-like lobes, narrowly lance-shaped, 2-4 in on flowering stems (to 5 in lower), hairy, mid-green; rays 40-100, purple (some pink), disc yellow to orange, heads about 1.5 in; stems branch near the top into a leafy corymb-like panicle; lower leaves dead by bloom; seed heads fluffy tan to brown pappus in fall and persist; spring shoots lance-leaved and green, come up through brown leaf litter. No measured proportions (head zone, width at head height, leafy share) because no whole-clump photograph was found that could be measured honestly.
Leaf colour: Mt Cuba trial (cultivars, 2009) calls the foliage grayish-green; the plan says mid to light green. Judge by eye.
